title: Maximum Sum With at Most K Elements
summary: Given a grid of size n x m, an array limits of length n, and an integer k, find the maximum sum of at most k elements from the grid where the number of elements taken from the i-th row does not exceed limits[i].
statement: Given a grid of size n x m, an array limits of length n, and an integer k, find the maximum sum of at most k elements from the grid where the number of elements taken from the i-th row does not exceed limits[i]. Return this maximum sum.
constraints: grid is a nonempty positive-integer matrix and limits has one value per row.
Choose at most k cells total and no more than limits[i] cells from row i.
hints: Only the largest limits[i] values of a row can belong to any optimal selection.
Collect those row-eligible values while retaining only the global k largest in a min-heap.
Sort each row descending, feed its allowed prefix to the heap, and pop whenever the heap exceeds k.
Any excluded row value is dominated by an included value from the same row, and the heap then enforces the remaining uniform global limit.
editorial: Any excluded row value is dominated by an included value from the same row, and the heap then enforces the remaining uniform global limit.

tests.explanation: The second row permits two selections, so taking four and three gives the maximum sum seven.
The global limit permits only the value nine.
